text.p: British health technology group Amersham International Plc said on Tuesday its planned merger with Norway's Nycomed ASA would give it world leadership in the fast-expanding field of diagnostics.
"The goal is to be the leader in in-vivo diagnostics," Amersham chief executive Bill Castell told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We see the opportunity in that market place growing significantly as biological science skills are applied to good chemistry," he added.

Castell, who will also be London-based chief executive officer of the combined Nycomed Amersham Plc, said the use of ultrasound techniques being developed by Nycomed would transform the way in which the body was scanned for diseases in areas like the liver, heart and kidneys.
Nycomed hopes that its lead ultrasound agent will be submitted for approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration next year.

Ultrasound, already used to provide images of unborn babies, holds promise in a number of areas where use of x-rays would be harmful, and Castell said this market could be worth 1 billion stg by 2005.

Castell said changes in technology were enabling doctors to look at the structure of the body and how the body was functioning. Amersham said the technique promised rapid diagnosis of heart problems and the spread of tumours in the liver, leading to much prompter use of surgery.
He said it would also be increasingly important as the drug industry develops highly-targeted drugs based on the way genes behave and interact in the body both to cause and combat diseases.
"Diagnostics and treatment are going hand in hand," said Castell.
Dr Peter Knox, Amersham's group chief scientist, added that: "Nycomed are at the top with a superb new product." He said the company also had an excellent patent position in its products.
Knox told Reuters that Nycomed's strength in ultrasound would be added to Amersham's existing strength in cardiology imaging, where its heart-imaging agent Myoview was seeing rapid growth in sales.

Amersham said the combination with Nycomed would strengthen both companies' world sales position, with Nycomed's strength in North America complementing Amersham's position in other regions, notably Japan.
"This give us a one-stop shop in the U.S.", where the company would be able to provide hospitals with nuclear, ultrasound and traditional x-ray technology, Knox said.
Castell said the two companies had started talks on a possible merger 12 months ago, but added that "we have got to know each other well over the years".
